en: Mount Apo, located in Mindanao, is the highest mountain in the Philippines with an elevation of 2,954 meters.
Taal Volcano is unique because its main crater is located on Volcano Island inside Taal Lake.
The Cagayan River, flowing through the Cagayan Valley, is the longest river in the Philippine archipelago.
Laguna de Bay, situated between the provinces of Laguna and Rizal, is the largest lake in the Philippines.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippines, located in the northern part of the archipelago.
The Tamaraw, a small hoofed mammal, is an endangered species endemic only to the island of Mindoro.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a massive, navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
The Sierra Madre mountain range runs along the eastern coast of Luzon and protects the island from Pacific typhoons.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippine Sea, part of the western Pacific Ocean, lies directly east of the main Philippine archipelago.
The Philippine Eagle, one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world, is endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
The San Bernardino Strait separates the Bicol Region of Luzon from the Eastern Visayas, connecting the Philippine Sea to the Sibuyan Sea.
